items.title: Section: The Five Things Ignorance Generates, Starting with Doubt About Who We Really Are

items.zh: 復次，無知，略於五處為能生因。一、能生疑，二、能生愛，三、能生非處信，四、能生見，五、能生增上慢。於前際等所有無知，是能生疑。謂如是疑：我於過去為曾有耶？為曾無耶？如是等疑於三世轉。如經廣說。過去名前際，未來名後際，現在名前後際。待過去世是後際，待未來世是前際故。若疑過去，當知此疑前際無知所生；若疑未來，當知此疑後際無知所生。若於內疑惑此誰所有？我為是誰？今此有情從何而來？於此沒已當往何所？當知此疑是前後際無知所生。
items.en: Next, not-knowing is, in brief, a generating cause with respect to five things. First, it generates doubt; second, it generates craving; third, it generates misplaced faith; fourth, it generates wrong views; fifth, it generates overestimation. Not-knowing concerning the prior period and the rest is what generates doubt — doubt such as this: did I exist in the past, or did I not exist? Such doubts turn across all three times, as extensively explained in the sūtras. The past is called the prior period; the future is called the later period; the present is called both the prior and later period. This is because, relative to the past, it is the later period, and relative to the future, it is the prior period. If one doubts the past, this doubt should be understood as generated by not-knowing the prior period. If one doubts the future, this doubt should be understood as generated by not-knowing the later period. If one doubts inwardly — whose is this? who am I? where has this being come from? where will it go once it perishes here? — this doubt should be understood as generated by not-knowing both periods.

items.title: Section: How Ignorance Breeds Craving, and a Modern Story of Trading One's Eyes for Thirty Years of Fortune-Telling

items.zh: 又於內無知、於外無知、於內外無知，當知能生內外等愛，及後有愛、喜貪俱行愛、彼彼喜樂愛。又若於業無知、於異熟無知、於業異熟無知，是諸有情由於業自造無知為緣故，於魯達羅天、毘瑟笯天、世主天等非正處中，生妄勝解，歸依、敬信。
items.en: Also, not-knowing the inner, not-knowing the outer, and not-knowing both inner and outer should be understood to generate inner and outer craving and the rest, together with craving for future existence, craving bound up with delight, and craving that eagerly seeks this or that pleasure. Also, if beings do not know karma, do not know its ripened result, and do not know the connection between karma and its result, then, through this very not-knowing about their own self-created karma as condition, they place false confidence, refuge, and devout faith in improper objects such as the god Rudra, the god Viṣṇu, or the lord of the world.

items.title: Section: Sixty-Two Wrong Views, and the First Kind of Overestimation — Starving, Burning, or Leaping to Reach Heaven

items.zh: 又若於佛等無知，乃至於道無知，當知能生諸見。所以者何？由於三寶及四諦中不正通達故，乃至能生六十二見；及起如是見，立如是論；無施、無愛，乃至廣說所有邪見。又若於因無知、於因所生法善不善等無知，廣如經說。由此無知故，於往善趣道、往善趣方便中，生增上慢。所以者何？由於善不善等法、愛非愛果不如實知故，於自餓、投火、墜高巖等非方便中起方便想，行如是事，以求生天。
items.en: Also, not-knowing the Buddha and the rest, up through not-knowing the path, should be understood to generate wrong views. Why? Because of failing to properly comprehend the Three Jewels and the four truths, up to generating the sixty-two views, and giving rise to such views, establishing such doctrines as: there is no giving, no love that bears fruit, and so on as extensively explained among all such wrong views. Also, if one does not know the causes of things, nor whether the phenomena produced by those causes are wholesome or unwholesome, as extensively explained in the sūtras — because of this not-knowing, overestimation arises regarding the path to a fortunate rebirth and the means of reaching it. Why? Because wholesome and unwholesome phenomena, and their pleasant or unpleasant results, are not truly known, one conceives self-starvation, throwing oneself into fire, or leaping from a high cliff as genuine means, though they are not, and carries out such acts in pursuit of heavenly rebirth.

items.title: Section: Venerable Sudarśana's Rainmaking Pride — Mistaking Meditative Power for Arhatship

items.zh: 又於六觸處中所有無知，於不如實通達得沙門果中起增上慢。所以者何？由實無有於六觸處如實通達智而生增上慢故。當知此中，若生天方便增上慢，若沙門果增上慢，總合此二名增上慢。
items.en: Also, not-knowing what actually occurs in the six fields of contact gives rise to overestimation regarding one who has not truly attained a contemplative's fruit but believes he has. Why? Because, lacking any genuine wisdom that truly comprehends the six fields of contact, overestimation arises precisely there. It should be understood that both overestimation regarding the path to heaven and overestimation regarding a contemplative's fruit are together called overestimation.

items.zh: 如是無明能生五種雜染。謂疑雜染、愛雜染、信解雜染、見雜染、增上慢雜染。由疑雜染所雜染故，一切愚夫獲得疑惑，信順於他引趣異路，於現法中，多受苦惱不安隱住。

items.title: Section: Four More Downstream Harms, from Denying All Cause to Wasted Effort on the Path

items.zh: 由愛雜染所雜染故，引生後有生老病等一切大苦。由信解雜染所雜染故，或謂無因，或計自在天等不平等因謂為正因，撥無一切士用而住。由見雜染所雜染故，隨意造作一切惡行，能感當來諸惡趣苦。由增上慢雜染所雜染故，令士夫用異果、無果。復此緣起善巧，如本地分已廣分別；所餘緣起善巧決擇，文不復現。
items.en: Because of being defiled by craving's defilement, one draws forth all the great suffering of future birth, old age, sickness, and the rest. Because of being defiled by misplaced faith's defilement, one claims either that there is no cause, or that some unequal cause, such as a creator god, is the true cause, and dwells in the denial of all human effort. Because of being defiled by views' defilement, one freely commits every unwholesome deed, thereby drawing forth the suffering of future miserable realms. Because of being defiled by overestimation's defilement, one's effort yields either a different result or no result at all. Next, the skilful understanding of dependent origination has already been extensively analysed in the Basic Section; the remaining decisions concerning the skilful understanding of dependent origination are not presented again here.

blocks.text: A short day: the five kinds of defilement that grow from ignorance.

Doubt, craving, misplaced faith, views, and overestimation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the present is both the later part of the past and the earlier part of the future. (Untranslated, 0612c18: through the defilement of doubt, the foolish fall into uncertainty, follow others down strange paths, and suffer in this life.)

Master Cháng Bǎi: inner craving is self-love for this life's body; craving for future existence is self-love for a future body. Not knowing that their karma is their own making, beings place faith in Rudra, Viṣṇu, and a lord of the world.
About the path to heaven, and about a contemplative's fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: without good deeds, how could one reach heaven?
Master Cháng Bǎi: some deny all human effort, holding everything to be without cause. Views lead to doing evil freely; overestimation makes effort bear the wrong result or none.
Formations, aggregates, elements, sense-fields, and the first part of dependent origination. The fascicle's centre is the analysis of ignorance: not a void but a cover, and a cover can be lifted.

quiz.q: Of what five is not-knowing a generating cause, and how are the periods divided?
options: craving, aversion, delusion, pride, doubt; the past later, the future prior, the present none, ceasing at once
the five aggregates; all three times being prior
doubt, craving, misplaced faith, views, overestimation; the past is the prior period, the future later, the present both
the five pure aggregates; all three being later
quiz.why: The treatise lists doubt, craving, misplaced faith, views, and overestimation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the present is the later period of the past and the prior period of the future, and so is called both. Of overestimation he says it is not that there is no practice, but that the understanding is mistaken.

quiz.q: Which cravings does not-knowing inner and outer give rise to, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: inner craving is for relatives, outer for friends, future for descendants, all family feeling unrelated to not-knowing
only one craving, for wealth
inner craving is self-love; future craving is for a coming inner body; relish for what is had; eagerness for what is not
all are wholesome aspiration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: inner craving is self-love towards this life's inner body, and craving for future existence is self-love towards a future inner body; craving with relish delights in objects already gained, and eager craving seeks objects not yet gained. These are the same four cravings as in fascicle 55.

quiz.q: What arises from not-knowing karma and its ripening?
options: right faith in the Three Jewels, those ignorant of karma needing faith, so not-knowing leads to good
greed for wealth
fear of death
false confidence, refuge, and faith in improper objects such as Rudra, Viṣṇu, and the lord of the world
quiz.why: The treatise says that from not knowing that one's karma is self-created, beings place false confidence and faith in Rudra, Viṣṇu, and the lord of the world. Master Cháng Bǎi: faith arises in unreasonable places outside the Dharma, not knowing that spirits have not severed afflictions and have only small powers. The English does not say that 世主天 means Brahmā.

quiz.q: What are the two overestimations, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: regarding heaven: self-starvation and the like as means; regarding the fruit: taking the temporary subduing of greed in absorption as attainment
regarding wealth and regarding learning, both pride in worldly possessions, unrelated to practise
the pride of ordinary and noble beings
pride of past and future
quiz.why: The treatise names overestimation regarding the path to heaven and regarding a contemplative's fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi: without good deeds how could one reach heaven, and with afflictions unresolved one still falls; and when absorption merely presses down greed, hatred, and delusion, one takes this as attainment, though the seeds of affliction are not severed.

quiz.q: The English has "denying and dwelling apart from all human effort" for 撥無一切士用而住. What is the problem?
options: 住 means dwelling in a monastery apart from people, so "dwelling apart" is right and unrelated to views
住 means abiding in this view of denial, not living apart from effort; both no-cause and unequal-cause theories exclude human effort
士用 means soldiers' use
撥無 means pushing afflictions aside
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: they deny all human effort and the function of phenomena, holding all to be without cause; theories of unequal cause and of no cause share the fault of excluding human effort. So 而住 means abiding in that stance. "Dwelling apart from all human effort" suggests a way of living, and "a creator god" narrows 自在天等.

quiz.q: What harm follows from the defilement of view and of overestimation?
options: view: wasted effort; overestimation: freely committing evil, the proud being most prone to it
both lead to heaven
both lead to buddhahood
view: freely committing evil, bringing evil-destiny suffering; overestimation: effort yielding a different result or none
quiz.why: The treatise says defilement by views leads to freely doing evil and suffering in evil destinies, and defilement by overestimation makes human effort bear a different result or none. Master Cháng Bǎi: however hard one practices, there is no fruit, and the effort is wasted; this flows from overestimation. The treatise's passage on doubt is missing from the English.
